name: g_AbilityKind1_ItemByAbility
summary: The Item-command table: 14 bytes, ability 368 + i maps to item 240 + i (items 240..253). It carries item ids, not abilities, and it is the only table that pairs an Item-command ability with its item.

behavior.text: Unit_ListItemCommandItems is the only direct reader: it accepts abilities 368..381, loads a row as a byte and writes the byte into the item list.

Action_BuildCurrentAction reaches the same rows through an address derived as this base minus 0x170, with no range check; an index outside the 14 rows reads the real bytes that follow the table (0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 255) rather than a zero.
items 254 and 255 are consumables by category and have chemist rows, but they have no row here, so the Item menu cannot offer them.

the paired ability must also have animation and effect rows and must be reachable from the item skillset's 16 slots, so a consumable needs an item record, a chemist row and a paired ability that is in this table and has those rows.
extending the table alone does not widen the mapping: the reader's range check and its byte-wide item output are the binding limits.

notes: V: the sheets Unit_ListItemCommandItems and Action_BuildCurrentAction.
open_questions: ? the purpose of the six bytes after the 14 rows; one out-of-range reader can reach them, but no stock ability is meant to.

name: g_AbilityKind2_ThrowCategory
summary: The Throw table: 12 equip-category bytes, ability 382 + i maps to one category. It stores categories, not item ids; an item is throwable when its record's equipment category matches a row for one of the unit's throw abilities.

behavior.text: the 12 bytes are equip categories, one per Throw ability in ability order 382..393; category 0 does not occur.

three functions read it: sub_140281488 matches the item's category byte against the unit's throw abilities; Unit_ListThrowableItems builds the category set for abilities 382..393; Ai_SurveyTargets starts one byte into the table and walks abilities 383..392.
no item id is stored in the table; the id comes from the caller's scan over the inventory, which stops at 255 in the throw list and at 0x100 in the AI search.
category 0 never appears, so an item whose category byte is 0 is never throwable even when every other condition holds.
the throw list also requires a weapon slot, weapon flags bit 1, a non-enemy unit and a non-zero count, so a category match is one of five conditions, not the only one.

notes: V: the sheets sub_140281488, Unit_ListThrowableItems and Ai_SurveyTargets.
open_questions: ? why the AI reader offsets by one byte and so never considers ability 382 or 393's category row.

summary: int16 length of g_RuntimeJobList (signed compares in the fill loop)

name: g_SaveAutoSlot
summary: The auto-slot record, one 0x9CE4-byte slot. The resume header import copies its summary fields into it, and the classic list exposes it as list slot 0.

name: g_SaveBattleSnapshot
summary: The battle snapshot buffer: 668,112 bytes of sparse live battle state (unit table, tile table, scene-task records, action state) captured for a kind-1 resume payload.

behavior.text: the payload builder copies this block and the materialiser copies it back.

name: g_SaveCheckpointCopy

behavior.text: the resume payload copies 40,164 bytes to this block and the kind-0 body is byte-identical to it.

name: g_SaveManager
summary: The save object SaveSlots_LoadFromFile takes (a pointer to the auto-slot object, see Save_ResumeCheckpoint). +888 gates New Game + and Music Player on the title menu (I: game cleared); +889 / +890 let the mode select start Classic / Enhanced at once (UILauncher_OnMenuAction buttons 112 / 110).

name: g_SaveRequestManager
summary: The save-data request object the slot, settings and PNG code queues work on. The same object carries the file object's request list and the per-area write/read kicks.

name: g_SaveSlotCache
summary: The fifty-slot image in memory: 50 records of 0x9CE4 bytes, the same bytes the PNG container carries. The slot screens read and write this cache, and the frame step copies it to and from the manager image.

behavior.text: the image-to-cache step moves 0x1EA488 bytes; the clear step fills it with 0xFF.

name: g_SaveWorkCurrent
summary: The live work copy of the running game, one 0x9CE4-byte slot record. The checkpoint helpers move it to and from the checkpoint block.

behavior.text: one end of the checkpoint and slot-pack moves.

name: g_SaveYoxPage
summary: The 1 MB 16-bit image page carried after a battle snapshot. It is compressed into the payload on write and inflated back here on load.

behavior.text: the page is written with a 0x800-byte row stride and inflated on load.

name: g_SceneIdWord

name: g_SceneObjectList

name: g_SceneTaskSlots
summary: Nine scene-task data records of 0xA8 bytes, parsed from u16 token streams during the battle map setup and captured in a kind-1 snapshot.

name: g_SceneUnitSlots
summary: The 16 scene-unit records (stride 0x548); the in-use dword is 8 bytes before each.

name: g_ScreenFade
summary: The fade and skip state: the low dword is the fade alpha, the high dword the skip state (0 none, 1 requested, 2 skipping).

name: g_SelectedCharaSkin

name: g_SelectedShopIndex

name: g_SelectedUnitIndex
summary: The selected unit index the item, shop and equip screens read as their unit argument (sub_140287D9C, sub_1402D7640, sub_1403331F8, sub_140333FE0, sub_140366FE0).

behavior.text: sub_140287D9C and sub_1402D7640 take the unit from this word rather than from their arguments.

name: g_SellScreenActive
summary: Non-zero while the sell screen owns a list; the row price helper returns 0 without reading the list while it is zero.

behavior.text: sub_14036C468 refuses to price a row when this word is zero.

name: g_ShopModeGate
summary: Global mode word that gates the shop and den badge refresh; the badge routine runs only while it is non-zero.

behavior.text: what the mode word selects; the sheet leaves it open.

name: g_ShopOrderGroup
summary: The buy and sell screens' current order-group byte; cleared when a screen's list is first bound so the list starts in its default order.

behavior.text: sub_14036A9D8 and sub_14036C49C clear it before building their rows.

name: g_ShopRowCallbacks
summary: The buy screen's row handler table (0x141876AD0 through 0x141876B00): one handler per row column, filled at first entry to the screen.

behavior.text: sub_14036A9D8 fills it through the list binder.

name: g_ShopScreenInitFlag
summary: One-shot setup byte of the buy and sell screens: the first entry builds the rows, later entries keep the existing list and scroll position.

behavior.text: sub_14036A9D8 and sub_14036C49C test it before building.

name: g_SkipRequestSource
summary: The skip-request source: its high dword is copied into the fade/skip state by the event runner. It is part of how a held skip action becomes a skip state.

name: g_SnapshotLookPool
summary: The look pool's copy in the battle snapshot region (0x2FA8A bytes, 15 records); Battle_RestoreSceneVars copies it back to g_LookPool.

name: g_StatusGroupMasks

name: g_StatusGuestMask
summary: 5 bytes (the values 0xEF 0x00 0x31 0x79 0xE2): the statuses a unit whose +0x1B4 byte is negative (a guest or special unit) can still receive. Status_FilterPendingSets ANDs it into the pending-add set for such a unit; no other reader

name: g_StatusIconFlags
summary: The per-status flag words the status panel update reads: index status+1, no bound check. Entries past 40 exist, so a forty-first status reads a meaningful but unintended value.

behavior.text: the status update switches on the id and reads this table in its default case.

name: g_StatusIconTileX
summary: Tile x of the status/item icon the status screen last set, copied from the icon state.

behavior.text: sub_1403932C8 copies it out of the icon state.

name: g_StatusIconTileY
summary: Tile y of the status/item icon the status screen last set, copied from the icon state.

behavior.text: sub_1403932C8 copies it out of the icon state.

name: g_StatusIconWord
summary: The packed page-and-palette word of the status/item icon the status screen last set.

behavior.text: sub_1403932C8 copies it out of the icon state.

name: g_TextCommandSlot
summary: The callback slot the battle text command installs: sub_140243390 is stored here and every branch of the text dispatcher calls it.

behavior.text: sub_140243330 writes the slot and then calls the dispatcher.

name: g_TextPoolTable
summary: The thirty-two text-pool pointers the generic decoder indexes by a text id's five kind bits. Slot 0 is filled at load and slots 1..31 by one loop.

name: g_TextureTable
summary: Engine texture table: handle -> texture object at +8 + 8 * handle (unit sheets, LUTs).

name: g_TrackedDateCounters
summary: uint8[64]: one counter per tracked date slot, capped at 99; slot 0 counts the date held in event variables 95 and 96, slots 1..63 the {month, day} pairs at 0x1407B8130. Written by the daily calendar tick (sub_1402CCEE0) and the jump by N days (sub_14039DA58); read by the page of the second tavern list (sub_140376040) at index (entry >> 4); copied by the save pack and unpack, the checkpoint pair and the errand state copy (saved at +0x48C of the save work block); reset by sub_14033FB84.

name: g_TurnList
summary: 40 x 4 bytes: byte 0 = unit (bits 0..4, 31 = end) | 0x20 command 18 | 0x40 pending action | 0x80 ability bit 8; byte 1 = ability low byte; word +2 = time. Copied from the list TurnList_BuildForSelection builds; read by the panel (TurnPanel_*)

name: g_UIChosenItemId
summary: The 16-bit UI field that holds the item id the player picked in the shop list.

behavior.text: sub_14036AC74 stores the id taken from the shared list row here.

name: g_UIDataModule
summary: UI tunables created at 0x1400E1D30: +16 float 1.0, +20 float 1000.0, +24 float 0.4 = the hand cursor's per-frame follow factor (no other writer found).

name: g_UINameTable
summary: pointer to the interned UI name table (127 buckets of 16-byte slots, refcounted); used by UIName_Intern / UIName_ReleaseKey and 958 callers

name: g_UIStateFade

name: g_UnitEquipOverride
summary: Five override equipment words per unit, ten bytes per unit index: when the pair is non-zero the equip pickers use it in place of the unit record's own hand words.

notes: V: five words per unit, ten bytes per unit index, at 0x14184A680. sub_1402D6464 stores a non-flagged unit word here before clearing the slot; sub_1402D5B6C restores it on cancel; sub_1402D65D4 returns it to the inventory on commit. A bit-14 word can be stored here (the 0x8000 test does not reject it) but no stock writer produces one on a unit word.

name: g_UnitImageAspectOn
summary: 1 after VideoState_InitDefaults (the normal case): selects the 1.1408199 width factor in Video_OnResize / Video_RefreshState.

name: g_UnitImageAspectX
summary: Pixel aspect factor applied to the WIDTH of the unit image node: 1.0, or 1.1408199 while g_UnitImageAspectOn is non-zero.

name: g_UnitJobFlags
summary: The job flag block: 21 per-job new flags then 125 per-job-type disable flags (see UnitJobFlagsBlock); saved in the save file.

name: g_UnitLookPoolIndex
summary: Look pool index of each battle unit by its unit index (+444): written by SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry when it builds the unit's scene unit, read back by it on the resume path (load mode 1) and by sub_1401D46B0; inside the battle snapshot region at 0x1408167A0.

name: g_UnitSaveData
notes: V: the five equipment words of the 600-byte save record live at +0x0E, +0x10, +0x12 and at +0x14/+0x16 or +0x18/+0x1A (the hand pair is placed by equip category). PartyUnit_WriteBackToSave stores the party word raw; PartyUnit_FillFromWork copies the save word back and zeroes it when the full 16-bit word fails its 1..0x104 id test.

name: g_UnitSceneSlotIndex
summary: Scene-unit slot of each battle unit by its unit index (+444), -1 none: written by SceneUnit_BuildFromQueueEntry (a slot taken by another unit clears that unit's entry) and sub_14026A048, cleared by sub_140210AF0, read on the resume path; inside the battle snapshot region.

name: g_UserSituation
summary: pointer to the situation store UserSituation_TestCheck reads: a bank flag byte at +16 (bit 0), flag bytes at +72 / +152, dword counters at +24 / +104. Counter 0 >= 450 opens the tavern errands (situation 3220). Written by UserSituation_SetValue (event opcode 0xE9) and its flag twin (0xEA), saved with the game (SaveWork_PackFromLive)

name: g_ZeroPair

The UI renderer constructor and UIRender_PrepareLayers copy it into the two layer atlas shelves as the starting cursor (x, y) = (0, 0); AtlasShelf_Alloc copies it again when it opens a new page. Other code reads it as a zero vector.

summary: Pointer to a 640-byte scratch party record (unk_143749CA0). sub_140289894 copies the selected g_PartyUnits record into it, so its +0x54..+0x5D are a second copy of the five hand words.
